issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service typed as string forward reference may not resolve and breaks equality semantics
issues.detail: The field is annotated as the string "FrameProcessor" but FrameProcessor is not imported in frames.py. As a dataclass field annotation this is benign at runtime, but it signals an unresolved forward reference. More importantly, identity-vs-equality matters at service_switcher.py line ~237 (`frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`); confirm FrameProcessor does not define __eq__ in a way that breaks this comparison.

issues.description: Breaking API rename lacks deprecation shim for external consumers
issues.detail: RequestMetadataFrame was a public symbol in pipecat.frames.frames. Renaming it without leaving a `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` alias (or DeprecationWarning) will hard-break any external service implementations that import or isinstance-check the old name. The changelog notes it but provides no migration path.

issues.description: Behavior change: frame now propagates downstream past inactive services
issues.detail: Previously RequestMetadataFrame was always suppressed by ServiceSwitcher.push_frame. Now only the frame targeting the active service is suppressed; if a non-active-targeted variant ever reached push_frame it would escape downstream. Combined with STTService now pushing the frame downstream after handling, any STT service outside a ServiceSwitcher will leak this internal control frame into the rest of the pipeline.

issues.description: Dataclass without default makes the frame non-trivially constructible and may break subclasses
issues.detail: Adding a required `service` field to a ControlFrame dataclass means all call sites must pass it. The diff updates the one known caller, but any third-party code constructing RequestMetadataFrame() will fail with a TypeError. Consider `field(default=None)` plus a runtime check, or document the breaking constructor change in the changelog.

issues.description: Comparison uses `==` on FrameProcessor instances; identity (`is`) would be safer
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on default object equality. If FrameProcessor (or a subclass) ever overrides __eq__, two distinct services could compare equal and the frame would be incorrectly consumed. Using `frame.service is self.strategy.active_service` matches the intent (same instance) and is robust to future __eq__ overrides.

issues.description: No test asserts the frame is suppressed at the ServiceSwitcher boundary
issues.detail: test_metadata_emitted_on_service_switch verifies the targeted service received the frame, but there is no assertion that ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame does NOT escape downstream of the switcher. Given the new conditional suppression logic, a regression test confirming the frame is consumed at the boundary would lock in the intended behavior.

review.summary: The rename and targeted-service logic are coherent, but several concerns warrant attention before merge. The biggest risks are the silent public-API break (no deprecation alias for RequestMetadataFrame), the now-required `service` constructor argument breaking external callers, and the behavioral change of STTService pushing the control frame downstream (which can leak past pipelines without a ServiceSwitcher). The `==` comparison on FrameProcessor instances and the string-typed forward reference are smaller hygiene issues. Test coverage should also assert frame suppression at the switcher boundary.
